- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. ## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `75877cc2e26ac57966af4ec641c9f6c95ddf8a3a`
Local-runs: probe — `npm view` and `npm pack @objectstack/verify@18.0.0-next.0` into the scratch directory, to read the published `dist/index.d.ts` the removal is judged against; nothing built, run or re-run.

Read at 2026-10-13T10:51Z, adversarially, against AGENTS.md Prime Directives #10 and #12 and Post-Task Checklist step 3. Inputs: card #15953 (body and all 32 comments, among them slice 5's landing `6139508960`, this slice's claim `6140521245`, the round-1 report `6141945855`, the ruling A2 `6142005900`, the round-2 report `6143598072` and the ACCEPT `6143646554`, read as a claim); slice 5's record `6138334190` on PR #23150; PR #23236's body, file list and the net diff of `refs/pull/23236/head` against merge base `76815b9013` (10 files, +294 / −206, five commits including three merges of `origin/main`); the published tarball's declaration file and CHANGELOG; the check-runs on the head, read five times. The only local commands were `git fetch` / `diff` / `show` / `log` / `merge-base` / `ls-tree` / `grep` against the fetched ref and `origin/main`, the template print, `gh api` reads, reads of untouched `harness.ts`, `handle.ts`, core and service-analytics files at the head, the gate scripts and the workflows, and the one npm probe.

### ① Derived judgments

**The published surface: right, and the removal is the only change.** The published `18.0.0-next.0` `dist/index.d.ts` exports 126 names; `src/index.ts` at the merge base names the same 126 (set-equal, checked name by name), and between the publish commit `d889448b93` and the merge base `packages/verify` moved only in `parent-write-reach.test.ts`, so the tarball IS the merge base's surface. At the head `index.ts` names 125: `DashboardWindowProofOptions` gone, nothing added. The published signature is `runDashboardWindowProofs(stack, token, config, options?: DashboardWindowProofOptions)`; the head's source is `(stack, token, config)`, return type untouched; the only other source change reachable from the entry is the function's docblock paragraph. `laterBy` / `vary` / `uniqueFields` / `fixtureBody`: 0 hits in the published d.ts, exported from `derive.ts` only, and `index.ts` re-exports `derive.js` by name (`deriveCrudCases`, `fillRelationalRefs` and four types; no `export *`), so they cannot reach the entry; `FIXTURE_TAG` is a module-private const in each family. No other export changes shape: no type the report carries is touched. The dev's four-hunk d.ts diff is what the source diff predicts; nothing was rebuilt here.

**The ruling's grounds: right in direction, with one overstated sentence in the changeset.** No caller in the tree: `packages/cli/src/commands/verify.ts:411` and all three test calls pass three arguments; the other mentions are CHANGELOGs, the consumed note and the README. hotcrm cannot have one: it pins `^17.7.0`, and the tarball's own CHANGELOG lists the family first under `18.0.0-next.0` (`54f062b`), so no 17.x carries the function at all; the dev's grep of the clone (0 hits) is reported, not re-run. The second ground, tested against the resolution path: the family resolves the 13 presets once with `resolveFilterTokens(condition, { now: start, timezone, userId })` and compares fixture days against those edges, while the door (`service-analytics/src/dataset-executor.ts:127`) resolves the same tokens with `filterTokenContextFrom(context, new Date())` per request. A `now` on another UTC day than the server's moves the ground truth away from what a correct server answers, so on a correct server it yields `contradicted` for every preset whose edges moved (`today`, `yesterday`, the rolling three, a week, month, quarter or year edge when crossed) and the same verdict for the rest; it can never add a true finding. The changeset's "any `now` other than the current instant made every window read `contradicted`" is therefore too strong on two counts: a `now` on the same UTC day resolves identically, and on another day only the presets whose edges move contradict. The operative ground stands: every non-default value is either equivalent to the default or a false red. Could a caller have used it meaningfully against the in-process server, which reads the same process clock? No: a caller who moves the process clock (as the new pin does with `vi.setSystemTime`) moves `new Date()` in the family and in the door alike, so the default already follows it, and `now` could only add a disagreement. Removal loses nothing, and a declared knob whose only non-trivial effect is a false red is the trap Prime Directive #10's corollary names.

**The day-turn guard: right.** `start = new Date()` (`:575`); `startDay = todayAt(start)` (`:582`); `todayAt(now)` is `String(resolveFilterTokens('{today}', tokenCtx(now)))` with the same `timezone` and `userId` as the presets, and `day0 = todayAt(new Date())` (`:795`): same token context, same clock, same spelling (`asYmd` in core). The two differ only when the day turned between the two reads (a non-UTC principal is already `not-run` at `:783`, before the guard), so on a run that did not cross midnight the guard cannot fire and cannot hide a contradiction; once it fires, every later measure of the run is `not-run` with a detail naming both days, which is right, since the resolved edges are stale for all of them. Order inside `probeMeasure`: the timezone check, the control leg (`before0`, the widget's own unwindowed query), `day0`, the guard, then the 13 windowed `before` queries, the required-relation base records, the fixture rows (`:826` on), the read-back, the `after` queries and the existing end-of-probe guard (`:884`, unchanged). So no windowed query is asked and no fixture row of the measure is written under stale edges. One precision: a base record for a related object (`baseRecord`, `:729` for a `countField` reference and `:811` for a required relation) is a shared record the family wrote before this PR too, not a day-stamped fixture, and the `:729` one precedes `probeMeasure`; the pin's "writes no fixture" is measured as `days` undefined, which is exactly the measure's rows. The pin: `vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['Date'] })` after `bootStack` and `signIn`, so `start` is read on the frozen clock; the stack copy's `apiAs` moves the clock one day on its first call; `contextFor` (`handle.ts:630`, `dispatcher.resolveRequestScope`) and `seed` are in-process and never go through `apiAs`, `registered()` reads `stack.metadata`, and the fixture app has one object with no relation, so the first door call is the control leg, between `start` and `day0`, as the test's comment says. Frozen `Date` means no real midnight can touch it, every timer is real so the in-process server's async work proceeds, and `vi.useRealTimers()` runs in `finally`. Deterministic. Red without the guard: by the code, the measure would place its rows on `day0` and judge against `start`'s edges while the door resolves on `day0`, so each rolling preset reads one fixture row narrower, which is the shape the dev's ablation reports (`last_7_days` 4 against 5, `last_30_days` 9 against 10, `last_90_days` 13 against 14); the pin asserts `inconclusive` and 13 `not-run`, so that reading is `contradicted` and red. Not re-run here. The session token outliving the one-day jump is evidenced by that same ablation, whose run went through fixtures and windowed queries after the jump.

**The helper move: right, and the byte identity holds by reading.** `uniqueFields`: the text removed from all four families equals the `derive.ts` text line for line. `laterBy`: the three string copies read `Date.parse` first and return the input on `NaN || days === 0`; the shared body (delete-behavior's, with `string` and `unknown` overloads) returns the input on `typeof !== 'string' || days === 0` and then on `NaN`; for a string input every branch returns the same value, and the moved spelling is the same expression. `vary`: the three copies differed only in the letter inside `-u`, `-p`, `-w` plus `k`, and each family now passes its own `FIXTURE_TAG` (`unique-scope` `'u'`, `parent-write-reach` `'p'`, `dashboard-window` `'w'`), so each writes what it wrote; the number, date and phone branches never took the letter and take none now. `fixtureBody(body, objectDef, n, tag, full = false)`: the loop is the three copies' loop with `full` defaulted; every call site at the head is in `(…, n, tag[, full])` order: `unique-scope.ts:630` `(body, def, n, FIXTURE_TAG)`, `parent-write-reach.ts:651` and `:807` `(…, ++counter, FIXTURE_TAG)`, `dashboard-window.ts:640` `(…, ++counter, FIXTURE_TAG)` and `:829` `(…, ++counter, FIXTURE_TAG, wide)`, `derive.test.ts` `(body, def, 4, 'u')` and `(body, def, 4, 'w', true)`; `tag: string` and `full: boolean` are distinct types, so a swapped pair would not typecheck, and `TypeScript Type Check` is success on the head. `unique-scope.ts:683` `vary(source.base, ++variant, FIXTURE_TAG)` keeps its probe values. `delete-behavior`'s `fixtureBody` stays private, and its reason holds in the code: it suffixes a unique string with a plain `-n` (before an email's `@`) with no tag and no date, URL or phone branch, and it advances the date offset for a non-string date value (`laterBy(value, dates++)` with no `typeof` test); the shared helper would write the tag, move a date by `n` days and skip a non-string date's offset, so no parameter carries it without changing a value. It imports the shared `uniqueFields` and `laterBy`, both byte-equal to what it had. The dev's capture-plus-differential (3439 records PASS, control FAIL on tag `x`) and the `vary` ablation agree with this reading and were not re-run. `derive.ts` imports only `@objectstack/spec/data` and `./artifact-collections.js`: no cycle.

**The docs sentences: right.** README's API line reads `runDashboardWindowProofs(stack, token, config)`; its `inconclusive` row says "the UTC day turned after the run started", which covers both guards; the changeset's fix paragraph matches the guard's placement and detail. The consumed note `.changeset/pre/15953-verify-dashboard-window-family.md` is byte-equal to `origin/main`'s (blob `144d744b53` on both) and absent from the diff.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/15953-verify-dashboard-window-now-removed.md`: `@objectstack/verify` **minor**, summary `fix(verify)!:` (the PR title is the same line), `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, one ADR-0087 marker, the launch-window BREAKING line, one FROM to TO line carrying the one-line fix, and the guard's fix paragraph. Judged against Post-Task Checklist step 3:

- **The declaration.** `no` plus one arm of the closed pair; `(narrowing)` is BREAKING; `no (widening)` is the only malformed pair, so this one is legal. Carriers: PR body line 2 and the changeset agree; the claim `6140521245` says `Clause-②: no` without the arm, which the ruling `6142005900` superseded on the new facts and set as the seat's own. Right.
- **The level.** Removing a published export and a parameter is an accept-set narrowing, BREAKING, and ships `minor` under the launch-window convention as it stands at this head: `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` is armed and refuses `major` until GA (its own written end condition, #14043), ADR-0087's amended level half says a pre-GA retirement ships `minor` with the banner and the disposition, and the precedent the ruling graded against (`.changeset/pre/23072-meta-doors-closed-sets.md`, PR #23133) carries the same grade, banner and arm. `Check Changeset` and `Lint · docs & code guards` are success. Right. Whether the window has closed is not this PR's to judge.
- **The migration.** "FROM `DashboardWindowProofOptions` TO nothing (no replacement): drop the fourth argument, so `runDashboardWindowProofs(stack, token, config, { now })` becomes `runDashboardWindowProofs(stack, token, config)`" states the FROM to TO mapping and the one-line fix; an upgrading agent grepping either name after `TS2554` or `TS2305` lands on it. Right.
- **The marker.** `not-required (runtime-export-retired @objectstack/verify#DashboardWindowProofOptions)`. The category is for retired exports of a published entry, types included (its header names "functions, constants, classes and types"); the fourth parameter is not an addressable operand (the member limb is `Type.member` only) and the marker's prose names it. Exactly one marker; `check-adr-0087-registration` verifies it in CI. Right.
- **The dev's measured reason for the FROM-line form**, read in the gate's source: predicate 3 ("from-operands-named") refuses a FROM operand the marker does not name as out of range, and a call `name(...)` reads as `name`; predicate 1 ("retired-from-entry") refuses a named operand that is still exported at HEAD. The ruling's literal line (FROM on the four-argument call) therefore cannot pass, naming the function in the marker cannot pass, and the written line is the only gate-legal form that still carries the ruling's whole content. Right, and the ACCEPT's acceptance of this deviation is correct.
- **The consumed note left as published, `{ now? }` included: right.** Changesets v3 moves a consumed note under `.changeset/pre/` and re-reads it at the stable cut, so the stable `18.0.0` CHANGELOG will carry the family's entry with `{ now? }` and, in the same section, this slice's BREAKING entry retiring it: a true history of what `next` published, and the FROM to TO line is what the grep finds. Editing the consumed note would make the stable text disagree with the `18.0.0-next.0` CHANGELOG already on npm, and `check-empty-changeset` reds a merge-base changeset modified by a PR by design (the dev measured that red on the first push). A2 over A1 is right for the stable CHANGELOG.
- **`@objectstack/cli`**: untouched, and its one call passes three arguments; no changeset owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report `6143598072` (round 2, the newest): `open_questions` empty. Its deviations, each answered:

- **The FROM-line form**: answered in ②, the gate's only legal form.
- **A local `--no-verify` probe commit, undone, never pushed**: the branch holds five commits from the merge base (`59507b26a3`, three merges, `84dbd2dd6b`), no `tmp-probe` commit is reachable from any ref, and `--no-verify` appears in AGENTS.md only as the thing the merge-deferral step must never need; this commit was a throwaway on a non-merge tree, reset away, and the pushed commits behind it passed `pre-commit` and `pre-push`. A process note, not a contract matter; nothing reached the remote.
- **Zero label writes**: the PR carries `needs:contract-review` (the ACCEPT names that write as the seat's own) and no `skip-changeset`, which would be wrong on a diff that publishes. Right.
- **Main moving 11 commits after the last merge**: `origin/main` is 11 commits past the merge base, touching 95 paths; the intersection with the PR's 10 paths is empty and `packages/verify` is untouched there, so the queue's rebuild cannot conflict and no third merge is owed. Right.
- **The root pid files**: on the dev's container, not in the tree; the head tree holds no pid, log or scratch file. Post-Task Checklist step 7 holds for the repository; the files stay for a person, as reported.

**The out-of-scope note** (`delete-behavior`'s plain `-n` suffix on a unique required date, URL or phone value), carried and not filed: right under Prime Directive #10 as it stands. It is a reading with no repro, its consequence is a refused fixture that the family reports `not-run` (never a false verdict), so the claim stays as narrow as the enforcement, and it is noted in the PR's acceptance notes and in the private copy's docblock. ESCALATED to the seat, not a FAIL: "carried" needs a carrier. The landing note should name it as owed on the next push to `delete-behavior.ts`, the way slice 5's landing `6139508960` carried the two notes this slice delivered; a note carried nowhere is lost when the card closes.

**Added by this review, carrier none**: the changeset's "every window read `contradicted`" sentence (①) overstates; the operative ground is right and the text ships as a CHANGELOG line that errs toward caution. A note, not a FAIL.

**Check-runs on the head, read five times in this act, latest run per name, at the stamp above:** 40 names, all concluded: 32 success, 8 skipped, 0 failure, 0 in progress (the ACCEPT's "23 success, 6 skipped, 8 in progress" was an earlier reading of the same runs). Success: `Build Core`, `Check Changeset` (the re-run after the label write), `Check Documentation Links`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` (no governed path among the ten), `Lint & Repo Gates`, the eight `Lint ·` jobs (`Lint · docs & code guards` carries `check-adr-0087-registration` and `check-empty-changeset`), the four PR-shape guards, `Test Core` and its six shards (affected-only, so `packages/verify`'s suite with the new pins ran), the four `Type Check ·` jobs, `TypeScript Type Check` and `filter`. Skipped: `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size` on their `labeled` re-run (their first runs on this head were success), `Build Docs`, and the five roster skips on a PR run (`Console Pin Gate`, the dogfood matrix row, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, `Temporal Conformance`). No gate was re-run by this act. What the seat owes before the queue, none of it in this diff: the carry line for the `delete-behavior` note on the landing comment.
